events.region: Northern Campbell; Southern Campbell; Crook County Plains; Weston County Plains
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 11 AM TO 11 PM MDT FRIDAY DUE TO
GUSTY WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR NORTHERN CAMPBELL, SOUTHERN
CAMPBELL, CROOK COUNTY PLAINS, AND WESTON COUNTY PLAINS...

.Warm temperatures, humidities as low as 13%, and southwest winds
gusting to 50 mph ahead of an approaching cold front will create
widespread critical fire weather conditions Friday afternoon through
Friday evening. Southwest winds increase over northeastern Wyoming
after 10 am Friday morning with sustained winds of 25 to 35 mph and
gusts of 40 to 50 mph through the afternoon. Winds will shift to the
northwest after midnight as the front moves through. While some
showers may accompany the front, not expecting any widespread wetting
rains.

The National Weather Service in Rapid City SD has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* TIMING...From 11 AM to 11 PM MDT Friday.

* WINDS...Southwest winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 50 mph.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...As low as 13 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.

events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor coastal flooding expected. Water levels of 4 to 6.5
feet above the normal high tide line expected.

* WHERE...Southern Seward Peninsula Coast.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to 10 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...For Nome and Golovin, water levels are
expected to rise to around 6 feet above the normal high tide
line. In Nome, this can result in water approaching low-lying
homes in Belmont Subdivision with standing water expected in the
port area. For Golovin, water may inundate any beach property
but the roads, buildings and residences shouldn't be impacted as
the water remains below the berm. Water levels will peak Friday
afternoon and gradually drop, but remain above normal through
the weekend.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Significant coastal flooding expected. Water levels 5 to
7 feet above the normal high tide line expected for Hooper Bay.
Water levels 2 to 4 feet above the normal high tide line for
the rest of the Yukon Delta Coast.

* WHERE...Yukon Delta Coast, particularly Hooper Bay.

* WHEN...From 4 AM Friday to 10 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...In Hooper Bay, beach property, and the lowest
buildings will be inundated. The access roads to the airstrip
and the larger parts of town will likely be inundated and access
to the airstrip will be cut off. Elsewhere along the Yukon Delta
Coastline, beach property and the lowest lying roads may be
threatened. Water levels will peak around midday Friday in
Hooper Bay then drop during the afternoon. Be aware that water
levels will remain high during each high tide into the weekend.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Water levels peak with the high tides
Friday and then slowly decrease through the weekend. South to
southeast winds peak Friday with gusts up to 65 mph possible.
